I experienced this issue when running PM2 from bamboo. It appeared like process.env.HOME was not set. 
This can be solved by prefixing calls to PM2 with HOME = 'your/home'. So for example:
HOME='/home/user' pm2 restart all

Same problem when running PM2 via `cmd.run` in Salt. I'm using PM2 on CentOS.

My workaround was to use the `env` parameter to `cmd.run` to set the `HOME` environment variable (thanks @sias87!).

@Unitech I've seen this error on CentOS as well when using pm2 with Chef, similar to @drawsmcgraw.  Sounds like this problem is bigger than Windows.  Please consider reopening this issue.

I would not assume that `$HOME` is set.  It's unclear why you really need it.  I don't really want to use pm2 user preferences for a daemon.  I spent a few hours tracking this one down in Chef code that interacts with pm2.

@Unitech @steve-jansen For what it's worth, I couldn't use the `npm.installed` Salt module to install PM2. Something about one of its dependencies (can't remember which unfortunately) needing the `HOME` environment variable. Wound up prefixing the install command in the same way that @sias87 mentioned.

That's not a knock on PM2. It makes me wonder if the need for the `HOME` env variable is actually not coming from PM2, but one of its dependencies.
#604 looks very promising to solve this issue.
I am hitting this problem too using centos 6.5 under vagrant running it from puppet

+1. This causes issues for me when I try to start the application in init scripts.
The following can be used as a (hopefully temporary) workaround:

``` bash
HOME="${HOME:=/root}" "$PM2_BIN_PATH"/pm2 start $SCRIPT
```

@dareid is right, I had the same problem, when setting up instances on aws using the cloud init script, the home directory was not set (amazon linux instance)

If I connect via ssh to the server and execute pm2 manually its ok, but if I tell cloud init to switch to the user (I created in my cloud init script) to execute the "pm2 start server.js" command, then it fails because the home directory is undefined

I now set the home directory (in my cloud init script), the same way as I do for the environment and it works:
- export NODE_ENV=production
- export HOME=/home/www_user
